Welcome to UnityBotV4 setup

We're going to walk through every piece of configuration step-by-step, in plain language. You can't get it wrong — every field is validated as you type, and the NEXT button only enables when your input looks right.

What you'll need:

  • A Discord bot token (we'll show you exactly how to get one)
  • A Pollinations.AI API key (free, takes 60 seconds)
  • Optionally: a Discord channel ID, a list of approved Discord servers, and Supabase/Claude-Collab keys (skip if you don't know what these are — you can always add them later)

This setup writes a .env file next to bot.py. Nothing is sent anywhere — it stays on this machine.

Discord Bot Token

Required. This lets the bot log in to Discord as your bot user.

How to get your Discord token

  1. Open https://discord.com/developers/applications in a new tab.
  2. Click the blue "New Application" button (top right corner).
  3. Type a name (anything works — e.g., UnityBot), accept the terms, click "Create".
  4. In the left sidebar of the new application page, click "Bot".
  5. Scroll down to the "Privileged Gateway Intents" section. Turn BOTH of these ON:
    • MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT
    • SERVER MEMBERS INTENT
  6. Scroll back up to the "Token" section. Click "Reset Token" (this is normal — the token is only shown once).
  7. Click "Yes, do it!" to confirm.
  8. You'll now see a long string. Click "Copy" next to it.
  9. Paste it into the box below.
If you ever see the token shown again, that's because you just reset it. Don't reset it twice — copy it the first time. If you lost it, you can reset again any time.
Format: 50–100 characters, letters/numbers/dots/dashes/underscores only.

Pollinations.AI API Key

Required. This is what the bot uses to talk to the AI backend (where chat + image generation happen).

How to get your Pollinations API key (new gen.pollinations.ai stack)

  1. Open https://enter.pollinations.ai in a new tab.
  2. Sign in (Google / GitHub — first login auto-assigns the free "Seed" tier).
  3. Generate a new API key. You'll see two choices:
    • Publishable key (starts with pk_) — pick this for most setups. It's safe to use from clients, rate-limited at 3 requests per burst.
    • Secret key (starts with sk_) — pick this only if your bot is running on a server you fully control AND you want no rate limits. It can spend Pollen, so protect it like an admin password.
  4. Copy the key.
  5. Paste it into the box below.
If you have an OLD token from the previous auth.pollinations.ai portal (a 16-character alphanumeric string), you can leave the box below empty and fill the legacy fallback box instead — the bot will detect the format and use the old endpoints.
Format: starts with pk_ (publishable) or sk_ (secret), followed by 8–64 letters/digits.
I have a legacy 16-char token instead (click to expand)
Format: exactly 16 alphanumeric characters. Bot will use legacy endpoints and log a deprecation warning.

Claude CLI Bridge (optional)

Skip this step if you don't plan to use the Claude-CLI-to-Discord bridge. You can always come back later.

What this does

The bridge lets a separate Claude CLI session "be" Unity in one specific Discord channel — read messages there, post replies as Unity. If you don't know what this is, you don't need it.

How to get a channel ID

  1. In the Discord desktop or web app: User Settings (gear icon) → Advanced → Developer Mode — turn it ON.
  2. Right-click the channel name in the channel list → "Copy Channel ID".
  3. Paste it below. It's a long number (15–25 digits).
Format: 15–25 digit numeric ID. Leave empty to use the default placeholder.
Default 5050. Change only if 5050 is already in use on your machine.

Approved Discord Servers (optional but recommended)

Lock the bot to specific Discord servers — defense-in-depth so it doesn't get added to random servers and start chatting there.

How to get a server (guild) ID

  1. Open Discord (desktop or web).
  2. User Settings (gear icon) → Advanced → Developer Mode — turn it ON (if not already on).
  3. In the left sidebar, right-click the SERVER ICON (the round/square icon for the server, not a channel).
  4. Click "Copy Server ID".
  5. Paste it below. To add multiple servers, separate them with commas (no spaces) — e.g. 123456789,987654321.

Want to disable DMs?

Add the special token no-dms to your list — e.g. 1234567890,no-dms. With no-dms present, the bot will ignore DMs entirely.

Leave empty to allow the bot in every server it's invited to. Recommended for production: explicit allowlist.
Format: comma-separated server IDs (digits only, no spaces). Add no-dms to disable DMs.
Restrict to specific CHANNELS too (click to expand)

If set, even inside approved servers the bot only responds in these channels. Get channel IDs by right-clicking the channel name → Copy Channel ID.

Format: comma-separated channel IDs (digits only, no spaces).

Review & Save

Here's everything we're about to write to .env. Secrets are redacted by default. Click "Save & Continue" to finalize.
